summary: Nicolas Tournadre is a scholar in linguistics and Tibetology who earned his PhD from Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Claude Hagège. He held positions at INALCO, Paris 8 University, the University of Provence, and Aix-Marseille University.
Nicole Baden works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Richard Baker, whom she succeeded in 2024.

Nicole Vandier-Nicolas was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and art history. She taught Chinese art at the École du Louvre (1958–1977) and served as professor of Chinese civilization at INALCO (around 1969–1976).

Niels Ludvig Westergaard worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Copenhagen, Bonn (under Christian Lassen), Paris, London, and Oxford, later serving as professor and Rektor at the University of Copenhagen.
Nigel Allan, working in history and archaeology, succeeded Marianne Winder and served as Curator of Oriental Books and Manuscripts at the Wellcome Trust (attested 1993).

Niharranjan Ray studied at Calcutta, UCL, and Leiden. A scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, he served as Bageswari Professor of Fine Arts at the University of Calcutta and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study.
Nika Jovic is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her master's degree at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, having also studied under Géza Bethlenfalvy.
Nikita Yakovlevich Bichurin was a scholar in sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied at Kazan Theological Academy and worked at the Département asiatique from around 1826 to 1853.
Niklas Luhmann, working in philosophy, studied at the University of Freiburg, Harvard University, and Bielefeld University. He served on the faculty at Bielefeld University from around 1968 to 1993.

Nikolai Solmsdorf works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard, having also studied under Alexander von Rospatt, and held a post at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Linguist Nikolai Trubetzkoy studied at Moscow University and under August Leskien. He held academic posts at Sofia University (around 1920–1922) and the University of Vienna (around 1922–1938).
Nima Repper is an Indology scholar who served as a Wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiterin at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Nina Mirnig is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She has held posts at the University of Groningen, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, and the University of Vienna.

Ninian Smart was a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at Glasgow, Oxford, and SOAS. His main posts included Foundation Professor at Lancaster University (1967–1982) and J. F. Rowny Professor at UC Santa Barbara (1976–1998).

Nira Wickramasinghe is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at the University of Paris and the University of Oxford, and became Professor of Modern South Asian Studies at Leiden University around 2010.

Nirajan Kafle is an Indologist who completed his doctorate at Leiden University under Peter C. Bisschop. He held posts at the Nepal Research Centre, the University of Naples "L'Orientale", and Leiden University.
Niran Rajvamshi works in history, archaeology, and Indology. In 2018, he was affiliated with the National Archives of Nepal and served on the editorial board of the Documenta Nepalica Book Series.

Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti, an epigraphist and Indologist, studied at Calcutta, Paris, Berlin, and Cambridge. He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India, serving as Government Epigraphist and later as Director General of Archaeology in India (1948–1950).
Nirbhay N. Singh works in religious studies and psychiatry. He has held positions at Virginia Commonwealth University, the Commonwealth Institute for Family Studies, and Augusta University.
Nirmal C. Sinha served as the editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested in 1978 and 1988).
